props.gloss_en: for three transgressions [those of the mishna: nidda, challa, the lamp] women die in childbirth (yoldot)
R' Elazar: [for those transgressions] women die young (yeladot)
R' Acha: [women die] for the sin of laundering their children's excrement on Shabbat
some say: [women die] because they call the holy ark 'arana' (chest)
R' Yishmael b. Elazar: for two sins amei haaretz die -- for calling the holy ark 'arana'
...and for calling the synagogue 'beit am' (house of the people)
R' Yosei: three 'bidkei mita' (breaches/crucibles of death) were created in woman: nidda, challa, and lighting the lamp
and some report it: three 'divkei mita' (things that cleave to / hasten death)
one version accords with R' Elazar (pairing per Steinsaltz/Rashi: divkei mita, hastened death, matches his 'die young')
and one accords with the Rabbis (pairing per Steinsaltz/Rashi: bidkei mita, the crisis of childbirth, matches their 'die in childbirth')
RSbG: the laws of hekdesh, terumot and tithes are themselves the bodies of Torah
...and they were handed over to amei haaretz
R' Natan: for the sin of vows a man's wife dies
as it is said: 'if you have nothing to pay, why should He take your bed from under you?' (Prov 22:27)
for the sin of vows children die (when they are young)
Rebbi: as it is said: 'do not let your mouth bring your flesh to sin... why should God be angry at your voice and destroy the work of your hands?' (Eccl 5:5)
Rebbi: which is the work of a man's hands? say: his sons and daughters
for the sin of neglecting Torah [children die]
the verse for neglect of Torah: 'in vain have I smitten your children; they took no instruction (musar)' (Jer 2:30)
Rav Nachman b. Yitzchak: for the vows position too, from here -- 'in vain (lashav) have I smitten your children': over matters of vanity
one said: [children die] for the sin of mezuza
for the one who says mezuza: a verse is expounded by the one before it, and not by the one before that
for the one who says neglect of Torah: a verse is expounded by the one before it and by the one before that
